item.title: Index for a mutation loop
item.description: arXiv:2610.18940v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Motivated by the 3d-3d correspondence, we introduce an index $\mathcal{I}_g^\phi$ for a mutation loop $\phi$ of a quiver and an integer $g \geq 0$. We prove its integrality $\mathcal{I}_g^\phi \in \mathbb{Z}$ under certain conditions, which extends the integrality conjecture of Gang--Kim--Yoon for $3$-manifolds to the broader framework of mutation loops in cluster algebras. Our index also has an interpretation as the genus-$g$ partition function of a $(1+1)$-dimensional TQFT. We provide explicit computations for mutation loops of period one. In particular, in the case of the generalized Kronecker quivers, we give an explicit formula expressing the generating function of the indices for all genera $g$ as a ratio of polynomials. Altogether, we provide a new insight to the interplay between the geometry of $3$-manifolds and cluster algebra.
item.dc:creator: Tsukasa Ishibashi, Yuji Terashima

item.title: Symplectic extension graphs and Ribet's lemma
item.description: arXiv:2610.19434v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $p$ be an odd prime, and let $\rho\colon G\to \GSp_{2n}(\Z_p)$ be an irreducible symplectic residually multiplicity free representation. We define the symplectic extension graph $\Gamma_\rho^\GSp$ associated with $\rho$ to be the directed graph whose vertices are the residual factors of $\rho$ and a directed edge between two vertices corresponds to a nonsplit extension between the vertices realized by $\rho$. Using the Euclidean Bruhat--Tits building associated with $\GSp_{2n}(\Q_p)$, under some assumptions, we prove the existence of certain paths in $\Gamma_\rho^\GSp$ and show that $\Gamma_\rho^\GSp$ is a disjoint union of nonempty strongly connected subgraphs. Moreover, we provide examples to show that the result we obtain is optimal.
item.dc:creator: Aniruddha Sudarshan

item.title: Uniqueness of twisted linear periods over Archimedean division algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.19875v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\DD$ be $\R$, $\C$, or $\HH$, and let $H=\GL_p(\DD)\times\GL_q(\DD)$ be the block diagonal subgroup of $G=\GL_{p+q}(\DD)$. We prove that $\dim\Hom_H(\pi,\eta)\leq1$ for every irreducible Casselman--Wallach representation $\pi$ of $G$ and every smooth character $\eta$ of $H$.
item.dc:creator: Yufeng Li, Junyan Xiao

item.title: Gaudin from Cherednik
item.description: arXiv:2610.20146v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $W$ be a complex reflection group and $X$ the De Concini-Procesi wonderful model of its reflection arrangement. Inside Etingof's sheaf of Cherednik algebras on $X$ we define a subsheaf generated by the Dunkl operators that extend the standard ones on the hyperplane complement. We conjecture that at $t=0$ the image of the logarithmic vector fields in a natural module over this subsheaf is the sheaf of Gaudin algebras on $X$ defined by Aguirre, extending a construction of Bonnaf\'e and Rouquier from the hyperplane complement to $X$. We prove the conjecture for $W=S_{3}$.
item.dc:creator: Matthew McMillan

item.title: Universally extendible characters
item.description: arXiv:2610.20520v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let theta be an ordinary character or a Brauer character of a finite group N. We show that theta extends to every overgroup $G=G_\theta\trianglerighteq N$ if and only if Z(N) <= Ker(theta) and the deflated character of Inn(N) extends to Aut(N)_theta. This equivalence is compatible with fields of values. A similar investigation for extensions from subnormal subgroups leads to a new characteristic subgroup of N.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin Sambale

item.title: Reductions of Galois representations of slope $2$
item.description: arXiv:2610.19293v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $p$ be a prime $\ge 5$. We determine the semisimplifications of the mod $p$ reductions of irreducible two-dimensional crystalline representations of the Galois group of ${\mathbb Q}_p$ of slope $2$ and weights $k\ge3p+4$ with $k \not \equiv 6 \bmod (p-1)$. The proof relies on the compatibility between the $p$-adic and the mod $p$ Local Langlands Correspondences for $\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb{Q}_p)$.
item.dc:creator: Eknath Ghate, Sudipta Majumder

item.title: Bicolored Eulerian quasisymmetric functions, affine lengths, and Theta operators
item.description: arXiv:2610.19363v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce a $q$-analogue of the bicolored Eulerian quasisymmetric functions by incorporating an additional grading arising from affine length, obtained by interpreting bicolored permutations as affine permutations. We also provide an intrinsic description of this refinement in terms of bicolored permutations by introducing notions of alignments and crossings, together with an explicit bijection identifying these statistics with the alignments and crossings in the existing literature. Finally, we prove that our refinement is symmetric by expressing it in terms of the Theta operators appearing in the Theta coinvariant Conjecture and the modified Macdonald symmetric functions. Assuming the Theta coinvariant conjecture implies the Schur-positivity of our refinement.
item.dc:creator: Hsin-Chieh Liao, Hai Zhu

item.title: Prefixes of Coxeter elements are Coxeter elements of the reflection subgroups they generate
item.description: arXiv:2610.19755v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $(W,S)$ be a Coxeter system of finite rank, let $T$ be its set of reflections and let $c \in W$ be a Coxeter element. For $x$ in the interval $[1,c]_T$ of the absolute order, let $P(x)$ be the subgroup generated by the reflections $t\le_T x$. We prove that $x$ is a Coxeter element of $P(x)$ with respect to the canonical Coxeter generators of $P(x)$, that $P(x)$ is generated by the factors of any reduced reflection factorization of $x$, and that the Hurwitz action on the reduced reflection factorizations of $x$ is transitive. The proof reduces the general case to the case of a Coxeter system whose Coxeter matrix has entries in $\{1,2,3,\infty\}$, which was treated by Hubery and Krause.
item.dc:creator: Patrick Wegener

item.title: On the Fomin-Kirillov algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.20033v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Fomin-Kirillov algebras $\mathcal{FK}_n$ are shown to be infinite-dimensional for $n\geq 6$. By computer calculations, we find an explicit nonzero primitive element of degree 14 in the identity component of $\mathcal{FK}_6$. For every $n\geq 6$, the existence of such an element implies that $\mathcal{FK}_n$ contains a polynomial subalgebra and is therefore infinite-dimensional, and that the canonical homomorphism from $\mathcal{FK}_n$ onto its associated Nichols algebra is not an isomorphism.
item.dc:creator: Yang Zhang

item.title: Degeneracy graph determinants and higher-dimensional Young diagrams
item.description: arXiv:2610.20368v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Kemp and Ramgoolam proposed a basis of monomials for a commutative semisimple algebra with generators \(C_1,\ldots, C_L\), constructed from a degeneracy graph which records how the eigenspaces of \( C_1\) are successively split by \( C_2,\ldots, C_L\). They showed that the basis property is equivalent to the non-vanishing of the determinant of the matrix of values of these monomials on the projector basis, and conjectured a factorised formula for this determinant, as a product of powers of eigenvalue differences. We prove this formula for any number of generators. The proof uses graph analogues of Newton polynomials. Their evaluation matrix is not triangular in general, but expanding the rows of the children of each node of the penultimate layer in a Newton basis of their eigenvalues makes it block triangular, with diagonal blocks given by smaller degeneracy graphs in which the final layer is removed. The formula then follows by induction on the number of layers. We show that the exponents in the determinant are overlap volumes of higher-dimensional Young diagrams attached to the nodes of the graph: intervals, ordinary Young diagrams, plane partitions and their higher analogues. Finally, the block triangular structure gives an explicit recursive inversion of the evaluation matrix, expressing the projectors in the monomial basis.
item.dc:creator: Sanjaye Ramgoolam, Micha{\l} Studzi\'nski

item.title: Arithmetic Siegel--Weil formula on the product of modular curves
item.description: arXiv:2610.20575v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove the full generating series arithmetic Siegel--Weil formula on the product of two modular curves, with arbitrarily singular coefficients. This is the case $\operatorname{GSpin}(2,2)$ in Kudla's program.
item.dc:creator: Ryan C. Chen, Baiqing Zhu

item.title: Mutation of {\tau}-exceptional pairs and sequences
item.description: arXiv:2402.10301v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce a notion of mutation for $\tau$-exceptional sequences of modules over arbitrary finite dimensional algebras. For hereditary algebras, we show that this coincides with the classical mutation of exceptional sequences. For rank two algebras, we show that mutation of $\tau$-exceptional sequences is transitive if and only if mutation of support $\tau$-tilting modules in the sense of Adachi-Iyama-Reiten is transitive.
item.dc:creator: Aslak B. Buan, Eric J. Hanson, Bethany R. Marsh

item.title: Stability of plethysm coefficients and modified polynomial induction
item.description:
arXiv:2610.07929v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $h_n$ denote the complete homogeneous symmetric function of degree $n$, $s_
u$ the Schur function indexed by a partition $
u$, and $\langle\cdot,\cdotangle$ the Hall inner product. The plethysm coefficient $\langle h_n[h_m], s_
uangle$ is the multiplicity of the Weyl module $W_
u(\mathbb{C}^N)$ in $\mathrm{Sym}^n(\mathrm{Sym}^m(\mathbb{C}^N))$ whenever $
u$ has at most $N$ parts. For a partition $\lambda$, let $\lambda[mn]=(mn-|\lambda|,\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\dots)$. Bowman and Paget proved that $\langle h_n[h_m], s_{\lambda[mn]}angle$ is independent of $m$ and $n$ once $m,n\ge|\lambda|$. We prove that this coefficient is already constant for $m\ge\lambda_1$ and $n\ge\lfloor(|\lambda|+\lambda_1)/2floor$, and that its stable value equals $\langle s_\lambda, H[H-1-h_1]angle$, where $H=\sum_{i\ge0}h_i$; the proof uses the skewing operators adjoint to multiplication by complete homogeneous symmetric functions. We give a short new proof of the Bowman-Paget theorem based on stability of vector-partition functions, which count the ways of writing a vector of non-negative integers as an unordered sum of non-zero such vectors (its parts). Using a Vandermonde-type determinantal identity, we deduce that the stable value is a signed sum of numbers of vector partitions all of whose parts have entries summing to at least 2. The same method gives a short proof of Brion's stability theorem. We show that the stable value equals the multiplicity of $W_\lambda(\mathbb{C}^k)$, where $k=\lfloor|\lambda|/2floor$, in an explicit representation of $GL_k(\mathbb{C})$ independent of $m$ and $n$, obtained by modifying the polynomial induction of Narayanan, Paul, Prasad and Srivastava. Finally, we prove an explicit positive formula for the stable value, which counts the number of lattice points in a polytope, when $\lambda_1\le 4$.
item.dc:creator: Soumyadip Sarkar

item.title: A Counterexample To The TF-cone Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.14814v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The TF-cone conjecture of Asai and Iyama predicts that the TF equivalence class of an integral $g$-vector is the open cone generated by the canonical summands of all its positive multiples. We give a counterexample to this conjecture. For the tensor product of the three-arrow Kronecker algebra with the path algebra of $s\to t$, a vector $w$ has a two-dimensional TF equivalence class, whereas every positive integral multiple $mw$ is generically indecomposable. The cone generated by these canonical summands is therefore a single ray. The same example disproves the relative-interior version proposed by Haerizadeh and Yassemi.
item.dc:creator: Jindong Yan, Shenglin Zhu

item.title: Non-Equivalence of Smooth and Nodal Conformal Block Functors in Logarithmic CFT
item.description: arXiv:2509.07720v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $\mathbb V$ be an $\mathbb N$-graded, $C_2$-cofinite vertex operator algebra (VOA) admitting a non-lowest generated module in $\mathrm{Mod}(\mathbb V)$ (e.g., the triplet algebras $\mathcal{W}_p$ for $p\in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 2}$ or the even symplectic fermion VOAs $SF_d^+$ for $d\in \mathbb{Z}_+$). We prove that, unlike in the rational case, for $N\geq 4$ there is no vector bundle on $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{0,N}$ whose fibers are the spaces of conformal blocks associated to certain $\mathbb{V}$-modules, since the dimensions of these conformal block spaces differ between smooth and nodal curves. Consequently, the sheaf of coinvariants associated to these $\mathbb V$-modules on $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{0,N}$ is not locally free for $N\geq 4$. It also follows that, unlike in the rational case, the mode transition algebra $\mathfrak A$ introduced by Damiolini-Gibney-Krashen is not isomorphic to the end $\mathbb E=\int_{\mathbb X\in \mathrm{Mod}(\mathbb X)}\mathbb X\otimes \mathbb{X}'$ as an object of $\mathrm{Mod}(\mathbb{V}^{\otimes 2})$.
item.dc:creator: Hao Zhang

item.title: Weak del Pezzo surfaces are characterized by the existence of $2$-tilting bundles
item.description: arXiv:2510.26199v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For $d\geq1$, a tilting bundle on a regular proper $d$-dimensional variety over a field is called $d$-tilting if its endomorphism algebra has global dimension $d$, the smallest possible value. We prove that, over any field, the existence of a $d$-tilting bundle implies that the anticanonical bundle is semiample and big, and hence the variety is weak Fano. Moreover, the endomorphism algebra is $d$-representation tame. Conversely, every weak del Pezzo surface over an algebraically closed field of arbitrary characteristic admits a $2$-tilting bundle. Thus a smooth projective surface over such a field admits a $2$-tilting bundle if and only if it is a weak del Pezzo surface. This proves the variety case of Chan's conjecture, originally formulated in characteristic zero, and extends it to arbitrary characteristic. As an application, we construct a non-commutative crepant resolution (NCCR) of the anticanonical ring of any regular proper $d$-dimensional variety over any field admitting a $d$-tilting bundle. The NCCR is the endomorphism algebra of the pulled-back bundle on the total space of the canonical bundle. In particular, we obtain NCCRs of anticanonical cones over Du Val del Pezzo surfaces over algebraically closed fields of arbitrary characteristic. These NCCRs are the $3$-Calabi--Yau completions of the endomorphism algebras of $2$-tilting bundles on the minimal resolutions, extending the known construction for smooth del Pezzo surfaces to the Du Val case.
item.dc:creator: Ryu Tomonaga

item.title: Cluster algebra and quasimap quantum cohomology
item.description: arXiv:2511.09875v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We apply the abelianization technique to obtain an explicit ring presentation for the quasimap quantum cohomology of GIT quotients. As an application, for quiver varieties associated with oriented-acyclic quivers, we establish a cluster algebra structure on their equivariant quasimap quantum cohomology rings.
item.dc:creator: Yingchun Zhang, Zijun Zhou

item.title: The Symmetric Hit Problem in Four Variables: Relative Cohits and Stabilizer-Fixed Preimages
item.description: arXiv:2606.02626v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this work, we study the symmetric hit problem in four variables by analyzing the relative cohit space, defined as the kernel of the inclusion-induced map from symmetric to ordinary cohits. Theoretically, we establish that this relative space is isomorphic to a kernel in the first group cohomology of the permutation group and, equivalently, to an $\operatorname{Ext}^1$ kernel for the general linear group, equipped with a canonical action of the normalizer quotient. Furthermore, bypassing conditional descent hypotheses, we utilize explicit Lucas--Cartan identities to construct unconditional fixed Steenrod preimages for nontrivial stabilizers, resolving infinite families of monomials strictly above the minimal-spike weight. Using the ordinary and symmetric Kameko isomorphisms, we reduce the determination of complete bases in two generic degree families to exact calculations in degrees one, three, six, ten, and sixteen. We discover that universal relative vanishing fails: the relative space is non-trivially one-dimensional in degree fifteen and forms an indecomposable two-dimensional normalizer module in degree eighteen. In the family $5\cdot2^t-4$, the symmetric cohit dimension stabilizes at six and the relative dimension at one for $t\geq2$; in the family $7\cdot2^t-4$, they are four and zero for $t\geq1$. We give complete bases by explicit exponent formulas and prove Janfada's monomial implication in every degree of both families. A general numerical threshold determines the finite initial degree from which Kameko isomorphisms apply, and a direct-sum formula transports the entire symmetric hit basis.
item.dc:creator: Dang Vo Phuc, Peter V. Danchev

item.title: Kodaira fibres and wrapped Floer cohomology
item.description: arXiv:2609.23884v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $F$ be a singular fibre of a relatively minimal complex elliptic fibration with smooth total space, and let $\Omega$ be a nonvanishing holomorphic two-form near $F$. We show that a small neighbourhood of $F$ is a Weinstein domain for $\mathrm{Re}\,\Omega$ whose completion is a Legendrian surgery, with cocores obtained by completing holomorphic disks transverse to the components of $F$. For every coefficient field and every multiplicative bulk class, we compute the wrapped Floer cohomology of these cocores and prove that it is concentrated in degree zero. The cocores generate, so the bulk-deformed wrapped Fukaya category is equivalent to the category of perfect modules over an explicit algebra: a multiplicative preprojective algebra of affine type for the normal crossing fibres, and a quiver algebra with relations for types $II$, $III$ and $IV$. Applications include formality of the affine plumbing dg algebras; mirrors given by resolved affine surfaces at every classical bulk class for affine D, E and types II, III, IV; and mirrors given by quotient stacks of algebraic tori at root-of-unity bulk classes for the four affine stars.
item.dc:creator: Yanki Lekili

item.title: Exact sequences of representation categories of weak Hopf algebras
item.description: arXiv:2609.40298v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study exact sequences of representation categories of weak Hopf algebras over an arbitrary field. Given a sequence $A\overset{k}{\to} B\overset{\pi}{\to} H$, where $A$ and $B$ are weak Hopf algebras and $H$ is a Hopf algebra, we develop verifiable algebraic conditions on $k$ and $\pi$ under which there is an exact sequence $\mathrm{Rep}(H)\to\mathrm{Rep}(B)\to\mathrm{Rep}(A)$ of tensor categories in the sense of Brugui\`eres and Natale (2011). Along the way, we develop a generalization of the restriction of scalars functor for maps $\pi:B\to H$ between associative algebras satisfying a weakened multiplicativity constraint depending on a relatively separable subalgebra $B_r\subseteq B$, as well as a theory of kernels and cokernels for weak Hopf algebras. We, in particular, find that the cokernel of a weak Hopf algebra homomorphism $k:A\to B$ always exists, is a Hopf algebra, and the cokernel map is surjective when $A$ is connected. We conclude by studying examples of such exact sequences built from groupoids, formal ribbon extensions of quasitriangular weak Hopf algebras, and cocycled crossed products of a Hopf algebra acting weakly on a weak Hopf algebra.
item.dc:creator: Quinn T. Kolt

item.title: Equivariant noncommutative crepant resolutions and $G$-maximal modifying modules
item.description: arXiv:2610.11708v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $S$ be a Cohen-Macaulay normal domain containing a field $k$ with an action of a finite group $G$ with $|G|$ invertible in $k$. We prove that $G$-equivariant noncommutative crepant resolutions of $S$ induce noncommutative crepant resolutions of $S^G$ if the $G$-action is small. We also discuss similar results for equivariant maximal modification algebras. We introduce the notion of $G$-maximal modifying ($G$-MM) module, and we show that $G$-MM module over $S$ induces MM $S^G$-module in some special cases. Furthermore, we prove that Gorenstein MMAs of three-dimensional $\mathbb{Q}$-Gorenstein Cohen-Macaulay rings are derived equivalent. As an application of these results, we prove the existence of an MM module and derived equivalences of MMAs for three-dimensional terminal singularities of index two.
item.dc:creator: Yuki Hirano

item.title: Harmonic Reduction of Spin-Coupled Grover Walks on Hypercubes via Quantum Bernoulli Noises
item.description: arXiv:2610.14467v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider spin-coupled Grover walks on hypercubes within the framework of quantum Bernoulli noises (QBN). We identify parity-dependent harmonic subspaces generated by the central Hamming layers: in even dimension they give a fixed-point subspace, whereas in odd dimension the walk reduces on the harmonic subspace to an explicit eight-dimensional reduced dynamics. Using symmetric-group representation theory, we characterize the corresponding isotypic structure and determine the reduced spectrum. The harmonic reduction also yields explicit long-time probability behavior and shows that the resulting states may occupy an asymptotically vanishing fraction of the hypercube while still spanning its full Hamming diameter.
item.dc:creator: Ce Wang
